A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 14-page RISE study, including supplementary Sections 8–10. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the text, equations, figures, tables and appendices.

before.justification: v3 reports original radar experiments, including object detection in Table 1, layout reconstruction in Figure 7, trajectory-length sensitivity in Figure 9 and component ablations in Table 2.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results, including object detection, layout reconstruction, trajectory-length sensitivity and component ablations.

M1.justification: The BAME processing, multipath inversion, hierarchical diffusion and inference-time spatial consistency optimization are identical, including the supplementary pseudocode and post-processing.

E1.justification: Both retain the same 11-environment RISE-Indoor benchmark and 35,000-floor-plan simulation corpus, covering layout reconstruction and object detection. No datasets, tasks or test scenarios change.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains BRL and EMT+SRHD as object-detection comparators. Layout reconstruction and trajectory-length comparisons retain EMT; comparator membership and adaptations are unchanged.

E3.justification: The collection and evaluation settings remain identical, including approximately 30-second trajectories, 20 Hz acquisition, ground-truth preparation, IoU/Dice metrics and the 15 cm F1 tolerance.

E4.justification: Figure 9 retains the same trajectory-length sensitivity analysis. Table 2 retains the ghost-enhancement, diffusion and reverse-optimization ablations, and Figure 8 retains the same qualitative comparisons.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point estimates and trajectory plots. Neither reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains RISE's 57.78% IoU and 69.34% Dice. Section 5.3 retains 16.03 cm Chamfer distance versus EMT's 39.06 cm, while Table 2 retains 16.32 cm for the full-model ablation. All plotted and qualitative results also match.

T1.justification: Equations 1–16 and their reasoning are unchanged, including the AOA/AOD formulation, spatial consistency objective and supplementary first- and second-bounce reflector derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about single-static-radar scene understanding, the benchmark, BAME, hierarchical diffusion and reconstruction/detection performance.

C2.justification: Results interpretations and Section 10's limitations are identical, including dependence on human motion, residual blind regions and restriction to 2D geometry.

D1.justification: Hardware, calibration, simulation and ground-truth processing descriptions are unchanged. Algorithm 1 retains the same thresholds, and no code or data access instructions are added or removed.

R1.justification: Reference [86] remains the same PAGE-4D work, updated from a 2025 arXiv entry to a 2026 ICLR entry. Its citation context in Section 2.1 is unchanged; no cited work or research-positioning argument is added or removed.

P1.justification: Reference [86] updates PAGE-4D's title, venue/year and author list, omitting Xinhai Chang. The arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 5 June 2026 to v4 dated 24 July 2026. Body prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Visual differences are confined to the updated and repositioned first-page arXiv margin stamp and local line wrapping within reference [86]. Figures, tables, captions and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revision updates one existing reference's bibliographic metadata and the arXiv stamp. Scientific evidence, explanations, reproducibility information and limitations remain identical, so these localized editorial changes produce no meaningful overall quality difference.
